Theorem
[Dirichlet's principle] 1. ch2:2.2-thm-17\group Energy Methods A function $u\in \mathcal A$ solves (46) if and only if \[ (47)\qquad I[u]=\min _{w\in \mathcal A}I[w]. \]
Proof

\sketch If $u$ solves (46), test against $u-w$ and integrate by parts. The identity

\[ \int _U|Du|^2-uf=\int _UDu\cdot Dw-wf \]

and $Du\cdot Dw\le (|Du|^2+|Dw|^2)/2$ give $I[u]\le I[w]$. Conversely, for $v\in C_c^\infty (U)$, minimality makes the derivative at $\tau =0$ of $I[u+\tau v]$ vanish:

\[ 0=\int _U Du\cdot Dv-vf=\int _U(-\Delta u-f)v. \]

Thus $-\Delta u=f$.

□
